title: Dundee Victorian microscope slides: Hornell & Sinel twenty-slide marine series and Watson & Sons foraminifera arrangement

primary_institutional_source.institution: University of Dundee Museum Collections — Zoology Museum
primary_institutional_source.source_status: institutional collection page with accession identifiers and object images

principal_upgrade.previous_state: A-level published maker examples; exact set architecture insufficiently separated from later Hornell subscription literature
principal_upgrade.new_state: Dundee directly identifies DUNUC2986 as part of a series of 20 marine-zoological microscope slides prepared by Hornell & Sinel. This closes institutional survival of a maker-attributed twenty-slide series at S level. The same page identifies DUNUC2999 as a Watson & Sons arrangement of 16 named Foraminiferans, providing a second direct commercial-object endpoint.

subscription_comparison_guard.reported_1893_scheme: The secondary research page reports that Sinel & Hornell's Microscopical Studies in Marine Zoology subscription began in November 1893 and offered fourteen microscope slides plus illustrated descriptive pamphlets for a prepaid annual subscription of 21 shillings.
subscription_comparison_guard.count_problem: Dundee's institutional series extent is twenty; the reported 1893 subscription extent is fourteen. These counts do not presently match.
subscription_comparison_guard.interpretive_consequence: Do not silently identify DUNUC2986 with Microscopical Studies in Marine Zoology. The Dundee twenty-slide set could represent a distinct commercial series, an expanded/later configuration, a composite set, or a museum reconstruction of series extent. Only slide labels, numbering, accompanying pamphlets, or a contemporary twenty-item list can decide.
subscription_comparison_guard.primary_source_locator: Natural Science volume 3 (1893) is available in the Biodiversity Heritage Library and Google Books; exact advertisement page/image remains to be extracted in a later bounded source pass.

secure_or_secondary_context: Sinel & Hornell operated a marine biological supply business in Jersey during the early 1890s and produced prepared slides.
A 1893 subscription scheme titled Microscopical Studies in Marine Zoology is documented in contemporary-advertisement research and later surviving publication history.
The Journal of Marine Zoology and Microscopy was published by the Jersey Biological Station in the 1890s; digitized volumes survive in the Biodiversity Heritage Library.
James Hornell's 1901 Microscopical Studies in Marine Zoology survives as a 124-page publication.
historical_business_context.guard: Business/publication context supports a plausible textual counterpart for Dundee's objects but does not itself identify the DUNUC2986 series.

analytical_payoff.series_form: Dundee supplies a compact surviving example of marine zoology distributed as a numbered/finite maker series, separate from the much larger mixed Gibson cabinet and from Cole's publisher-designed serial cabinet.
analytical_payoff.maker_vs_publication_problem: The current twenty-versus-fourteen discrepancy is analytically useful: maker series, subscription publication and museum series description may represent different address systems applied to related glass objects.
analytical_payoff.watson_comparator: DUNUC2999 gives a single arrangement slide whose epistemic unit contains sixteen named specimens; this differs from one-specimen-per-slide series and can test how commercial catalogues valued arrangement, naming and multiplicity.
